rationale:
Evidence: all three raced designs (iterations 0, 1 and 3) went off track in every development trial, with finish rate 0. Progress barely changes across designs: about 0.04 on the s-bend in every race, and 0.035 to 0.125 elsewhere. max_error sits at about 0.061 in every race, which is the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06). rms_error is about 0.03 and steering_oscillation is small (0.06 to 0.15), so the robot is not jittering. It drifts steadily to the edge and leaves.

What I learned: the 0.04 s-bend progress is almost identical across kp, kd, ki, sensor size and line-loss settings. That suggests a common failure point early in the course, most likely at a sharp entry bend that the robot takes too fast. Iteration 3 (adding ki = 0.6) moved the score only from 37.04 to 36.46, so integral action is not the fix. Iteration 2 (wide 7-sensor array with weights scaled to offset) was never raced, so its geometry is still unverified and should be tested now.

Changes: (1) Use the iteration-2 geometry: 7 sensors at x = -0.075 to +0.075 in 0.025 m steps, y = 0.06, sensor size 0.016. This keeps the tape visible out to about 0.09 m of offset, so the robot sees the line before it reaches the off-track limit. (2) Reduce base_speed from 1.2 to 0.9. This tests whether speed is the cause of the early failure, and it gives the steering more time to settle through bends. (3) Keep kp 4.5 and kd 0.4 from iteration 2, since the wider array halves signal per metre of offset. (4) Set ki to 0 to keep the test clean.

Expected result: the robot should hold the line through the early bend, so max_error should fall below 0.06 and progress should rise above 0.04 on the s-bend. Completion within 3 s is unlikely at this speed. If the robot now tracks to the end, the next revision should raise base_speed in steps toward about 1.5 to 2.0.
